chapter: Band family, war years and wrap-up
title: Keys to the city and plaques
summary: He has several keys and plaques from Birmingham.

story.theme_name: Late-career reflections: awards, legacy and life lessons
story.community_name: Being honored: NEA Jazz Masters and other awards

blocks.x: Now, you mentioned the fact that he's passing this key to you from the mayor of your hometown. Well, how does it feel to get a key to the city from your hometown? You know, it doesn't happen to everybody.
I have, let me see, one, two, three. I have about 4 keys. One is one little town out of Birmingham. The key that he last gave me, but I'm trying to think of the name.
But, I had different mayors, you know?

Different mayors. So, each one gave me a key when I'd go back. And then I, at the time, the last key that I got from Birmingham, they had a big outing for me. They gave me this plaque that they put up in Tuxedo Junction. And from there, they go to the park and they had a big concert. The band, the Birmingham band there played for the concert while we were getting ready for the concert that night. This was at midday. And the mayor, the senators who were there spoke. I'm not used to those, getting up in front of mayors and senators to make a speech.
But, I found something to say, you know. It was really wonderful. So, if you

could see my wall, you could see a lot of different plaques from the school, 'Bama State, Birmingham, Arts Hall of Fame in Birmingham, and different organizations there. I have a wall full. I have a few here. The rest of them are down at my home.
And, they showed their appreciation about me coming from Birmingham. I suppose. So, this has been really nice. They've been treating me real nice. I always get a chance to hear from them.
